items.title: Where Could Adobe's Next Growth Come From?
items.summary: Adobe’s revenue grew 12% over the last year, slower than most of its big software peers. The share price appears to assume that its growth is fading. Over the last year, the stock fell 35%, while the S&P 500 returned 17.7%. Adobe (ADBE) trades at 12.5 times its earnings, against 22.1 for the index. Management pointed to a small, fast-growing line on its fiscal Q3 2026 call. Is that going to be enough? Where could Adobe’s next real growth come from.

items.title: Prediction: Figma Stock Set for 25% Upside
items.summary: Figma shares sit near a 52-week low even as revenue growth keeps accelerating, leaving a glaring gap between price and fundamentals that either signals a rare buying opportunity or a warning investors are missing something critical.

items.title: What Is The Case For Waiting On CRM Stock?
items.summary: Salesforce (CRM) stock has gained about 44% over the past three months, while the S&P 500 rose 3.5%. Investors entering at current levels are buying after a substantial run-up. Consequently, the valuation places greater pressure on upcoming earnings to justify recent gains. Have you already missed the move in Salesforce stock.

items.title: The Right Time to Judge a New CEO
items.summary: There’s a question several corporate boards should be asking themselves about now.  New CEOs will take control at Adobe and Best Buy in the coming weeks.  Stanislav Shekshnia, a professor at the French business school INSEAD, argues that the right time for all of these companies to assess whether they picked the best candidate is about six to 12 months into the CEOs’ tenures, which is several years before most boards do so, he says.

items.title: The Reason To Buy Autodesk Stock
items.summary: Autodesk (ADSK) stock has fallen 23% since late August. A $10,000 holding bought at the high is now worth about $7,700. A fall that fast pulls you toward buying, but the shares still cost more than the market on earnings. The reason to buy is that past Autodesk drops this deep mostly paid off, and the business is still sound.
